- **Fix: "Done Paying" no longer hangs at "Starting session..."** â€” The session-start handler sent its response only AFTER running the blocking `aircoins-captive-rules auth <mac>` subprocess (which since v1.27.0 also starts the DNS forwarder). If that subprocess was slow, the portal stayed frozen on "Starting session...". The response is now sent first and the firewall/TC work runs in the background, so Done Paying completes instantly. The frontend also gained a 25s failsafe so the modal can never hang indefinitely.
- **Change: Post-payment redirect is now automatic (no modal)** â€” After a successful coin payment or voucher redemption, instead of showing a "Connected" modal with a button, the portal now auto-redirects the client to the configured post-payment URL (after a short 0.8s delay). No-op when no redirect_url is set.

- **Feature: Post-payment redirect / landing link** Ã¢â‚¬â€ A new "Post-Payment Redirect" setting in the Portal page lets the operator enter an absolute http/https URL (a landing page, thank-you page, promo link, or IP). When set, after a client finishes inserting coins and gains internet (or redeems a voucher), the portal shows a "Connected" modal with a button that opens the configured link in a new tab. Leave the field blank to disable (default Ã¢â‚¬â€ no behavior change).
- Backend: `redirect_url` added to the portal appearance config, validated as an absolute http(s) URL and persisted with the theme/colors. Backward compatible Ã¢â‚¬â€ old saved configs simply have no redirect.

- **Architecture: ISP-independent DNS for authorized clients (no more DNS lock-in)** ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â Authorized clients' DNS was DNAT'ed directly to the ISP's DNS server, with the ISP's IP frozen into each per-MAC iptables rule at authorization time. Moving the unit to another ISP left every rule pointing at a dead DNS, breaking all apps until a refresh. Now a second dnsmasq instance ("clean DNS forwarder") listens on port 5353: no captive hijack, no DHCP ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â it just forwards queries upstream using /etc/resolv.conf, which DHCP/systemd-resolved updates automatically when the ISP changes. Authorized clients' DNS is REDIRECTed to this local forwarder (iptables REDIRECT carries no IP at all), so per-MAC rules can NEVER go stale. Plug the unit into any ISP ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â clients' apps work immediately, no refresh needed.
- The forwarder service (`aircoins-dns-forwarder.service`) is created and started automatically by `aircoins-captive-rules` on first auth/refresh, and survives reboots.
- `refresh` now serves as a one-time migration: it rebuilds all tracked MACs' old ISP-DNS DNAT rules into forwarder REDIRECT rules. The boot DNS watcher (v1.26.8) and the manual Refresh DNS button remain as harmless safety nets.

- **Critical fix: DNS refresh was a silent no-op** ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â `aircoins-captive-rules refresh` compared the freshly detected DNS against `UPSTREAM_DNS`, but that variable is re-detected at the top of the same script run, so the comparison was ALWAYS equal and refresh always exited with "DNS unchanged - no refresh needed" without touching any iptables rule. This is why neither the automatic boot watcher nor the manual button restored internet after an ISP change. Refresh now unconditionally rebuilds the per-MAC DNS DNAT rules (and probe/forward rules) for every tracked authorized client with the currently detected DNS ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â rewriting an already-correct rule is harmless. This fix also makes v1.26.8's automatic boot watcher actually effective.
